goal: Build a small routes.json collector using current source data. First code-map {}, export-snapshot include ["routes.json"], read-source by sourceId, import-conventions with notes/sourceIds. Read output/case schemas. Get the exact /orders case entityId using get-capabilities schema=identity, kind=route, slots={scopeId:repo.repo.main,routerId:app,mode:history,declaredPath:/orders}. Never guess a hash. Use a Node script under 100 lines: JSON.parse current sources and emit each current JSON route with stable identity and real byte evidence; do not hardcode facts. Use includeIdentityHelper=true and identity.mjs in artifacts. File updates merge, so cases/inputs may be sent in subsequent write-candidate calls; omit nothing required before validate-plugin. Include ONE case requiring the exact /orders ID and its CollectorInput from export with stageId=extract. No file entities or relations needed. Validate and stop after activation.

investigation.notes:
Investigation (routes focus), evidence bound to Core snapshot snap_7d15edf4e81af2d47be21f345795042e53c033b1cdf92a71f61e30d97ab6eb94.

1) Route registry source: exactly one config source in scope — path `routes.json`, repositoryId `repo.main`, sourceClass `config`, contentHash ed7c08383e568fcdcbbe6daae45d60f4cc8c9534d04ba85e3524bcb292a3f102, byteLength 124 (declared/observed).
   Content: {"routerId":"app","mode":"history","routes":[{"path":"/orders","name":"Orders"},{"path":"/inventory","name":"Inventory"}]}\r\n
   (trailing CRLF; byte offsets are relative to this exact buffer.)

2) Declared route-registration convention (basis: observed, from routes.json bytes):
   - top-level `routerId` (string) = router instance id -> route identity slot `routerId`; observed value "app" at bytes ~15-20.
   - top-level `mode` (string) = history/hash routing mode -> route identity slot `mode`; observed value "history" at bytes ~30-39.
   - top-level `routes` (array of objects) each with `path` (declared path -> identity slot `declaredPath`) and optional `name` (business label attribute, NOT an identity slot).
   - No page/component binding, no title/i18n source, no alias entries and no menu registry exist in this snapshot; those remain coverage gaps rather than absent facts.

3) Route identity: kind `route`, canonical slots in order [scopeId, routerId, mode, declaredPath] per Core identity spec. Project id is the exported configSubset.projectId = "live-project"; scopeId used by Core for this case is "repo.repo.main".

4) Exact /orders entityId computed by Core (schema=identity, kind=route, slots={scopeId:repo.repo.main, routerId:app, mode:history, declaredPath:/orders}) => ent_d023c5b7b1847d6433677bfab770467189c7f74667609124f1f89523aff31a3f. No hash was guessed; same input must be fed to the identity helper so the script recomputes it per run.

5) Evidence plan: emit one evidence record per route object using real byte ranges located by string search over the current source content, with role "route-definition", plus one whole-file evidence with role "registry-document". IDs via computeEvidenceId(sourceId, contentHash, startByte, endByte, role) so they are stable and content-bound.

6) Refresh behaviour required by protocol: output must be recomputed from the input sources each run — adding a route adds an entity, editing routerId/mode/path invalidates the old entity id (previous ids disappear), which satisfies the source-change acceptance expectation without hardcoding an entity list.

7) Out of scope / gaps to declare in output: rules only recognise JSON registries shaped like routes.json; any non-JSON or differently shaped registry is reported as a coverage gap (code `unrecognized-route-registry`), never silently dropped.
